data.hook: Jeremiyah Love has pushed through a high ankle sprain all week, logging limited practices and team drills ahead of his potential NFL debut.
data.name: Cardinals Rookie Jeremiyah Love Questionable for Season Opener
data.summary: The Arizona Cardinals list third overall pick Jeremiyah Love as questionable for Sunday's game at SoFi Stadium against the Los Angeles Chargers due to his preseason high ankle sprain. Coach Mike LaFleur says Love is trending well after a solid week of limited work, with the expectation he plays, though it's a game-time decision. Even if active, the team plans to manage his snaps carefully alongside veteran Tyler Allgeier, while guard Isaiah Adams, safety Dadrion Taylor-Demerson, and cornerback Garrett Williams are ruled out.

data.hook: Ashton Jeanty's X-rays showed a clean bill of health, letting the Raiders running back celebrate his return to full practice ahead of Sunday's big game.
data.name: Raiders Get Jeanty Back, Rule Out Bowers for Dolphins Opener
data.summary: Running back Ashton Jeanty is cleared to play after a full week's practice with no injury designation, bringing a spark to the Raiders' backfield against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium. Tight end Brock Bowers, however, is out following a recent knee meniscus procedure, prompting coach Klint Kubiak to shift from early optimism to confirming he'll miss Week 1 but return soon. Fans and analysts noted frustration with the coach's initial outlook, while the healthy Dolphins roll into the matchup ready to go.

data.hook: Jim Harbaugh channeled Babe Ruth, pointing his prediction straight: Justin Herbert will one day stand as the NFL's top quarterback.
data.name: Harbaugh Predicts Justin Herbert as Greatest QB Ever
data.summary: On 'The White House with Michael Irvin,' Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh boldly forecasted that Herbert, the 28-year-old star with elite arm talent and mobility, will be remembered as the best to ever play QB. Herbert boasts a career-high 91.2 PFF grade from 2024 and strong passing stats since his 2020 draft as the No. 6 pick, though skeptics highlight his zero playoff wins and debates over his spot in Chargers history behind Philip Rivers. Harbaugh's praise fits his pattern of hyping his QBs, stressing the team's need to match Herbert's competitiveness as they gear up for 2026.

data.hook: A Dolphins fan flying to Vegas had a blunt take on the season opener: 'None.' Now Clelin Ferrell gets a shot at the Raiders who once drafted him fourth overall.
data.name: Dolphins Elevate Clelin Ferrell for Raiders Opener Amid Rebuild
data.summary: The Miami Dolphins called up edge rusher Clelin Ferrell from the practice squad to face the Las Vegas Raiders in their season opener at Allegiant Stadium. The former first-round pick out of Clemson brings 21 career sacks and veteran depth to a young defense, creating a personal revenge storyline against his original team. Entering a full rebuild with new GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, coach Jeff Hafley, and QB Malik Willis, the Dolphins face low expectations—including talk of an 0-17 season—making this a key test for the regime. Kickoff is 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX, with Miami as underdogs.

data.hook: Two rookies, Spencer Fano and Austin Barber, step into the Browns' starting offensive line for Sunday's opener, filling gaps left by injuries and marking the team's first full line change since 1990.
data.name: Browns Start 2026 with Rookie-Led Offensive Line Overhaul vs. Jaguars
data.summary: The Cleveland Browns face the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, with rookie left tackle Spencer Fano and rookie right guard Austin Barber starting due to injuries to Teven Jenkins (back) and a questionable Parker Brailsford (thumb). This creates an entirely new starting offensive line from last year's Week 1 group. Fano shared his excitement after practice, saying he and Barber focus on improving daily, while Barber prepared for his NFL debut by staying ready for any role. The Browns also elevated linebacker Nathaniel Watson and cornerback D’Angelo Ross from the practice squad, as the Jaguars deal with their own injury concerns like a questionable LeQuint Allen Jr. and limited Anton Harrison.

data.hook: With Ty Johnson sidelined by a hamstring tweak, the Bills called up familiar faces from practice squad to keep their backfield and returns humming Sunday in Houston.
data.name: Bills Elevate Gore Jr. and Dortch for Texans Opener
data.summary: The Buffalo Bills elevated running back Frank Gore Jr. and wide receiver Greg Dortch from the practice squad for their season opener against the Houston Texans. The moves address Ty Johnson's questionable hamstring injury, providing insurance behind starters James Cook and Ray Davis while Dortch handles punt returns. Dortch, who joined the team just 12 days ago after stints with the Cardinals and Lions, adds veteran explosiveness on special teams and as a slot option, helping ease in rookie Skyler Bell.

data.hook: Tua Tagovailoa grabbed his side after a throw in practice, ending his shot at Week 1. Now veteran backup Cooper Rush steps in for the Falcons' opener.
data.name: Falcons Turn to Cooper Rush as Starting QB with Tagovailoa Out
data.summary: The Atlanta Falcons named Cooper Rush their starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers after ruling out Tua Tagovailoa with an oblique injury from Thursday practice. Michael Penix Jr., still recovering from a torn ACL, will be the emergency option, with undrafted rookie Jack Strand as backup. Rush, a 32-year-old journeyman with a 9-7 record as a starter, faces a tough Steelers defense that racked up 48 sacks last season amid the team's ongoing quarterback carousel.

data.hook: Just when the Falcons thought their quarterback woes couldn't get wilder, starter Cooper Rush shook off back spasms Saturday and suited up for Sunday's clash with the Steelers.
data.name: Falcons' Cooper Rush Powers Through Back Spasms to Start Opener
data.summary: Rush steps in after Tua Tagovailoa's oblique injury sidelined him, with Michael Penix Jr. inactive from a torn ACL and undrafted rookie Jack Strand as backup. The team signed Rush in July amid a wave of injuries, and he's now set to lead the offense despite the group's recent interception troubles and zero snaps for Strand. Fans buzz with memes, like Kurt Benkert's quip about 'meatball subs left in the tank,' as the 32-year-old veteran—9-7 in 16 career starts—faces Pittsburgh's stout defense.

data.hook: R-Truth, the Charlotte-born WWE star and die-hard Panthers fan, pumps up the crowd in the team's cinematic 2026 season trailer. Arms outstretched in team gear, he delivers that signature energy just days before kickoff.
data.name: Panthers Unleash Hype Trailer with R-Truth for 2026 Home Opener
data.summary: The Carolina Panthers released their official 2026 season trailer on Thursday night, featuring longtime supporter and local hero R-Truth in dramatic visuals of hooded figures, flag-waving players, and field action. The promo hypes their home opener this Sunday against the Chicago Bears at Bank of America Stadium, with fans firing back phrases like 'Let’s fucking go' and 'WE READY!!!!' R-Truth's deep roots as a team ambassador add a personal spark to the excitement as the campaign kicks off.
